subject: music
title: Schoenberg and Dodecaphony
welcome_lead: 1923: a method of composing with twelve tones related only to one another.
meta_desc: A-Level Music: Schoenberg, atonality and twelve-tone technique.

concepts.def: Twelve-tone serialism, formulated by Schoenberg c. 1921-1923.
Ordering of the 12 chromatic pitches used as basis of a piece.
Four forms of the row — P, R, I, RI.

walkthroughs.body_html: From around 1908, Schoenberg wrote atonal works (e.g. Pierrot Lunaire, 1912). By 1923 he had codified twelve-tone composition: an ordered row of the 12 chromatic pitches forming the piece's basis.
The row is used in four forms — Prime (P), Retrograde (R), Inversion (I), Retrograde Inversion (RI) — each transposable to 12 levels: 48 forms in total.
Schoenberg's students Berg and Webern extended dodecaphony. Webern's pointillist textures and Berg's quasi-tonal lyricism showed the method's range; together they formed the Second Viennese School.

mcqs.q: Schoenberg's twelve-tone method was formulated around:
What is a tone row in serial music?
options: An ordered series of all 12 chromatic pitches, used as the basis of a piece.
A row of notes played together as a chord.
Any sequence of notes a composer chooses.

mcqs.q: What does the time signature 6/8 indicate?
options: Two beats per bar, each beat divided into three (compound duple).
Six beats per bar, all equal in stress.
Three sections: A, contrasting B, and a return to A (ABA).
